gallery.title: File:110725-F-HS721-350 (5977279566).jpg
gallery.artist: NATO Training Mission-Afghanistan
gallery.description: Afghan Minister of Interior Bismillah Khan Mohammadi, center, cuts a ribbon symbolizing the opening of the Afghan National Civil Order Police headquarters and stand up of the 5th Brigade at Lashkar Gah in the Helmand Province, Afghanistan, July 25, 2011. The minister was joined by the ANCOP and provincial police commanders, Provincial government leaders and elders and the Governor of Helmand, Gulab Mangal (far right). The headquarters opening and brigade standup come one week after the Afghans took over security control in the Helmand Province from coalition forces. (U.S. photo by Senior Airman Kat Lynn Justen)

gallery.title: File:131110-M-FN127-166 (10853306865).jpg
gallery.artist: U.S. Department of Defense Current Photos
gallery.description: U.S. Marine Corps Sgt. Maj. Paul A. Berry, center, the command sergeant major of Regional Command Southwest, speaks with Marines on the 238th birthday of the Marine Corps at Forward Operating Base Delaram II, Helmand province, Afghanistan, Nov. 10, 2013. (DoD photo by Cpl. Nicholas T. Nohalty, U.S. Marine Corps/Released)

gallery.title: File:131022-M-ZB219-152 (10607270385).jpg
gallery.artist: U.S. Department of Defense Current Photos
gallery.description: Afghan children sit next to a gas pump along a convoy route used by U.S. Marines with Combat Logistics Regiment 2, Regional Command Southwest in Helmand province, Afghanistan, Oct. 22, 2013. The Marines pushed out to Forward Operating Base Musa Qala to conduct resupply and backhaul operations during a five-day mission. (DoD photo by Cpl. Paul Peterson, U.S. Marine Corps/Released)

gallery.title: File:130718-M-YH552-232 (9340962465).jpg
gallery.artist: U.S. Department of Defense Current Photos
gallery.description: U.S. Marine Corps Lance Cpl. Joseph Nunez and Viky, a Marine Corps improvised explosive device detector dog, both attached to Fox Company, 2nd Battalion, 2nd Marine Regiment, search a compound for hidden threats during Operation Grizzly in Helmand province, Afghanistan, July 18, 2013. Grizzly was a counterinsurgency operation to deter enemy activity, establish a presence and gather intelligence. (DoD photo by Cpl. Alejandro Pena, U.S. Marine Corps/Released)

gallery.title: File:130410-M-SA716-024 (8643148490).jpg
gallery.artist: U.S. Department of Defense Current Photos
gallery.description: U.S. Marines with the 2nd Battalion, 9th Marine Regiment; British soldiers and Afghan National Army (ANA) soldiers, all with with Task Force 528, and ANA soldiers with Afghan Territorial Force 444, board a U.S. Marine Corps CH-53E Super Stallion helicopter with Marine Heavy Helicopter Squadron (HMH) 461 in Helmand province, Afghanistan, April 10, 2013. HMH-461 provided logistical support during a joint operation. (DoD photo by Sgt. Gabriela Garcia, U.S. Marine Corps/Released)

gallery.title: File:130409-M-BO337-027 (8636782087).jpg
gallery.artist: U.S. Department of Defense Current Photos
gallery.description: An Afghan Local Police member arrives to receive his first payment for his work as a policeman April 9, 2013, in Helmand province, Afghanistan. The Afghan Local Police was tasked with serving rural areas with limited Afghan National Security Forces presence. (DoD photo by Sgt. Pete Thibodeau, U.S. Marine Corps/Released)

gallery.title: File:130330-M-BO337-224 (8613108453).jpg
gallery.artist: U.S. Department of Defense Current Photos
gallery.description: A U.S. Marine with a Marine special operations team assists with security during a construction project for an Afghan Local Police (ALP) checkpoint in Helmand province, Afghanistan, March 30, 2013. The ALP complemented counterinsurgency efforts by assisting and supporting rural areas with a limited Afghan National Security Forces presence. (DoD photo by Sgt. Pete Thibodeau/Released)

gallery.title: File:130327-M-BO337-043 (8598628500).jpg
gallery.artist: U.S. Department of Defense Current Photos
gallery.description: Afghan Local Police recruits wait for the start of their graduation ceremony in Helmand province, Afghanistan, March 27, 2013. (DoD photo by Sgt. Pete Thibodeau, U.S. Marine Corps/Released)

gallery.title: File:130319-M-RF297-100 (8577858098).jpg
gallery.artist: U.S. Department of Defense Current Photos
gallery.description: Doc, an improvised explosive device detection dog (IDD) assigned to the U.S. Marine Corps 2d Combat Engineer Battalion, retrieves a bumper during a training session at Camp Leatherneck, Afghanistan, March 19, 2013. IDD handlers are matched with a dog and work together to perform route clearance and other duties in a combat environment. (DoD photo by Sgt. Tammy K. Hineline, U.S. Marine Corps/Released)

gallery.title: File:130102-M-RO295-012 (8362370503).jpg
gallery.artist: U.S. Department of Defense Current Photos
gallery.description: U.S. Marine Corps Staff Sgt. Cassie N. Winslow, left, a career planner with Regional Command Southwest, reads out a certificate of reenlistment during a reenlistment ceremony for U.S. Marine Corps Sgt. Maj. James M. Boutin at Camp Leatherneck, Helmand province, Afghanistan, Jan. 2, 2013. (DoD photo by Staff Sgt. Ezekiel R. Kitandwe, U.S. Marine Corps/Released)

gallery.title: File:121209-M-ZE895-010 (8292271582).jpg
gallery.artist: U.S. Department of Defense Current Photos
gallery.description: A Marine advisor to the Afghan Border Police braces himself prior to being engulfed in a cloud of dust in southern Helmand province, Afghanistan, Dec. 9. The sudden dust storm was caused by an MV-22 Osprey landing nearby.

gallery.title: File:120727-M-SF473-015 (7691953326).jpg
gallery.artist: U.S. Department of Defense Current Photos
gallery.description: A U.S. Marine Corps CH-53D Sea Stallion helicopter assigned to Marine Heavy Helicopter Squadron (HMH) 362 conducts a general support mission over Musa Qala district, Helmand province, Afghanistan, July 27, 2012. (DoD photo by Lance Cpl. Alexander Quiles, U.S. Marine Corps/Released)

gallery.title: File:120615-N-SF510-002 (7402827168).jpg
gallery.artist: U.S. Department of Defense Current Photos
gallery.description: U.S. Navy Construction Mechanic 3rd Class Cody A. Brown, assigned to Naval Mobile Construction Battalion (NMCB) 11, removes a drive shaft on a mine-resistant, ambush-protected vehicle in Helmand province, Afghanistan, June 15, 2012.  NMCB-11 was deployed to Afghanistan to conduct general, mobility and survivability engineering operations, defensive operations, Afghan National Army partnering and detachment of units in order to enable the neutralization of insurgency and support improved governance and stability operations. (DoD photo by Construction Mechanic 2nd Class Brandon Trumbo, U.S. Navy/Released)

gallery.title: File:120414-M-RK893-003 (7106829045).jpg
gallery.artist: U.S. Department of Defense Current Photos
gallery.description: U.S. Marines assigned to Marine Medium Tiltrotor Squadron (VMM) 365, 2nd Marine Aircraft Wing (Forward), pick up coalition forces in Helmand Province, Afghanistan, April 14, 2012. VMM-365 provides support of combat troops, supplies, and equipment during amphibious operations and subsequent operations ashore. (DoD Photo by Cpl. Marcus Kuiper, U.S. Marine Corps/Released)

gallery.title: File:111030-N-TH989-143 (6303396514).jpg
gallery.artist: U.S. Department of Defense Current Photos
gallery.description: A runner participates in the Marine Corps Marathon Forward at Camp Leatherneck in Helmand province, Afghanistan, Oct. 30, 2011. More than 300 coalition service members participated in the 26.2-mile marathon, which is a satellite edition of the Marine Corps Marathon in Washington, D.C. (U.S. Navy photo by Mass Communication Specialist 2nd Class Jonathan Chandler/Released)

gallery.title: File:111006-M-LU710-121 (6237448151).jpg
gallery.artist: U.S. Department of Defense Current Photos
gallery.description: U.S. Marine Corps Lance Cpl. Eric Devine, a personal security detachment team member, assigned to Regional Command (Southwest), walks to Helmand's Governor Mohammad Gulab Mangal's compound in Lashkar Gah, Helmand province, Afghanistan, Oct. 6, 2011. Devine was providing security for Regional Command leaders visiting Lashkar Gah for a reintegration shura or meeting. (DoD photo by Sgt. Mallory VanderSchans, U.S. Marine Corps/Released)

gallery.title: File:110716-M-SM240-581 (5964328531).jpg
gallery.artist: U.S. Department of Defense Current Photos
gallery.description: An Afghan National Police (ANP) officer stands in formation before the start of an ANP-led clearance operation outside of Lashkar Gah in Helmand province, Afghanistan, July 16, 2011. (DoD photo by Cpl. Adam Leyendecker, U.S. Marine Corps/Released)

gallery.title: File:110616-M-LU710-063 (5880460861).jpg
gallery.artist: U.S. Department of Defense Current Photos
gallery.description: U.S. Marine Corps Lieutenant Col. Sean Riordan, left, the commanding officer of 1st Battalion, 3rd Marine Regiment; and British Army Brigadier Nicholas Welch, right, the deputy commander of Regional Command Southwest (RC (SW)), greet an Afghan agricultural specialist as they walk through a marketplace outside Forward Operating Base Delhi in Garmsir, Afghanistan, June 16, 2011. Welch traveled from Camp Leatherneck, Afghanistan, with other military leaders from RC (SW) to perform a district deep-dive, a forum to explain in-depth information in each district the U.S. Marines represent, and to discuss progress and issues in the Garmsir District area of operations. (DoD photo by Sgt. Mallory S. VanderSchans, U.S. Marine Corps/Released)

gallery.title: File:110611-M-LU710-101 (5880432875).jpg
gallery.artist: U.S. Department of Defense Current Photos
gallery.description: U.S. Marine Corps Maj. Gen. John A. Toolan, commander, Regional Command (Southwest), visits an Afghan National Army post at Combat Operating Post Coutu, Helmand province, Afghanistan, June 11, 2011. Maj. Gen. Toolan traveled from Camp Leatherneck, Afghanistan, to conduct a battlefield circulation, or touring of a unit's area of operations, with leaders from 2/8, and discuss progress and issues in that area. (U.S. Marine Corps photo by Sgt. Mallory S. VanderSchans/Released)
